items.title: Lobbyists and trade groups fight to shape how states regulate medical AI

items.title: I’m a doctor. Here’s what I want the public to know about AI tools and health care costs
items.excerpt: “We can document honestly and still wind up inflating hospital bills,” writes a frustrated doctor.

items.title: Johns Hopkins Medicine taps OpenEvidence to bring AI into medical education, clinical care
items.excerpt: Johns Hopkins Medicine is teaming up with OpenEvidence to advance the use of artificial intelligence in medical education and clinical care.

items.title: Are Hospital Operating Rooms Ready For FDA’s Expectations for Surgical Robots?
items.excerpt: The FDA recently published draft guidance on pre-market testing for robotically-assisted surgical devices, raising timely discussion around whether hospital infrastructures are capable of supporting increasingly complex systems.

items.title: AI Can Flag Cognitive Decline Earlier — Health Systems Still Own What Happens Next
items.excerpt: Earlier detection is valuable, but it creates a duty that does not end when an alert appears in the electronic health record. Health systems need to decide, in advance, how a risk signal becomes a clinically accountable pathway.

items.title: Why Agentic AI Works in Hospitals When You Strip It Down
items.excerpt: Many hospitals are now trying to use AI to automate processes and free up staff time, running simultaneous pilots to perform as many tasks as possible. This quickly leads to pilot sprawl — a state where organizations can no longer even say which agents are still in active use.

items.title: Hidden signals in sleep can predict future health
items.excerpt: From a single night of sleep, AI tools can uncover physiological patterns linked to disease and mortality that are missed by conventional sleep measures.

items.title: MHRA 2030 Strategy to modernise patient-centred regulation for the era of AI and personalised medicines
items.excerpt: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has set out ambitious plans to translate cutting-edge scientific and technological innovation into better health outcomes for patients across all four nations of the UK, in its 2030 Strategy published today.

items.title: Bradford skin cancer waiting times cut by new AI technology
items.excerpt: Clinic can now see more patients and get results faster thanks to new scanning technology.

items.title: AI, Tech Leaders Are Lobbying Trump Health Officials in a Government-Run Chat Room - KFF Health News
items.excerpt: A Slack workspace managed by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services has served as an extraordinary war room for AI industry insiders and Trump administration officials to launch a rapid campaign aimed at persuading Americans to manage their healthcare and medical records on apps.

items.title: AI in Health Care Moves Toward More Autonomous Roles — The Monitor
items.excerpt: Federal health agencies are testing AI applications that move into patient care typically handled by physicians. And recent research suggests people may place more trust in conversational AI, while false claims attributed to authoritative sources can increase willingness to share them.

items.title: Physicians fire back against HHS secretary’s claim AI is ‘better informed’ than human docs

items.title: Brainomix adds patient input to e-Lung lung CT study
